【対象Topic】
Assigned Desks Are Back in Some Offices

【複数のSource(Claude Codeが既知URLへ直接アクセスして取得、またはWeb検索結果の要約として
取得したもの。それぞれのaccess_status/retrieval_methodを参照)】
[
  {
    "source_id": "SRC-001",
    "title": "Assigned Seating Is Slowly, Quietly Coming Back To Offices",
    "authors_or_organization": "Bisnow (reporting from Bisnow's New York Office Conference, with quotes from Scotiabank, iCapital Network, Rudin, and HubStar workplace-analytics data)",
    "publication_date": "2026-06-18",
    "journal_or_venue": "Bisnow (commercial real estate trade press)",
    "doi": null,
    "url": "https://www.bisnow.com/new-york/news/office/assigned-seating-returns-to-office-135073",
    "source_type": "TRADE_PRESS_NEWS_ARTICLE",
    "access_status": "FULL_TEXT_ACCESSIBLE",
    "retrieval_method": "DIRECT_FETCH_KNOWN_URL_NOT_SEARCH",
    "fetched_extraction": "Reporting from Bisnow's New York Office Conference (2026-06-18, 7 Penn Plaza) describes a trend of offices quietly bringing back assigned seating instead of unassigned hot-desking. Scotiabank's Global Head of Real Estate, Linda Foggie, is quoted: \"There's a slow, quiet shift that's happening, back towards more assigned seating and less flex seating.\" iCapital Network's Head of Global Real Estate, Gabrielle Rubin Deveaux, describes the shift as moving from \"rightsizing to optimizing.\" Rudin's Vice President of Asset Management, Jane Luger, proposed sharing building occupancy data with tenants. The article cites HubStar workplace-analytics data (based on more than 27,000 workplaces analyzed) showing enclosed/private offices rose from 4% of space in 2023 to 10% in 2025, and that conference rooms built for 17+ people show only 12% utilization while nearly 80% of meetings happen in rooms for 6 or fewer people; the current average is about 1 conference room per 8 desks (versus a traditional ratio of roughly 1 per 10-20 employees), and collaboration space now averages about 40% of workspace versus roughly 33% previously. The article also cites Gensler survey data (a survey of more than 16,000 employees): nearly 1 in 5 workers currently lack an assigned desk, and nearly 60% say they would prefer a personal workspace; among employees who do have assigned seating, 87% report a sense of belonging at work versus 74% in unassigned environments, and 80% with assigned seats say they can focus effectively versus 67% in hot-desking setups."
  },
  {
    "source_id": "SRC-002",
    "title": "Hot-Desking: Not So Hot with Employees",
    "authors_or_organization": "Korn Ferry (This Week in Leadership commentary, citing a review of workplace research and Gensler/Kastle Systems/Harvard Business Review data; named Korn Ferry contributors: Mark Royal, Ph.D., Maria Amato, Tamara Rodman)",
    "publication_date": "2023",
    "journal_or_venue": "Korn Ferry Insights (corporate advisory publication)",
    "doi": null,
    "url": "https://www.kornferry.com/insights/this-week-in-leadership/hot-desking-not-so-hot-with-employees",
    "source_type": "CORPORATE_ADVISORY_RESEARCH_SYNTHESIS",
    "access_status": "FULL_TEXT_ACCESSIBLE",
    "retrieval_method": "DIRECT_FETCH_KNOWN_URL_NOT_SEARCH",
    "fetched_extraction": "A Korn Ferry commentary states that a review of \"two dozen research papers on the topic\" concluded that \"flexible desking arrangements uniformly breed discontent\" (no specific institution or publication conducting this underlying review is named in the retrievable text, and no exact publication date for the review itself is given; treat the '24 studies' figure as a claim attributed to an unnamed review, not as a directly verified primary count). The article separately cites Gensler data that the share of employees using hot-desking arrangements has \"doubled, to 20%, since before the pandemic.\" It cites Kastle Systems data that roughly half of offices in major U.S. cities remain unoccupied on a given day. It cites a Harvard Business Review (2023) survey of 819 employees in which over half said they were trying to avoid \"unwanted interactions with colleagues\" by working from home, and a separate Gensler finding that 48% of workers cite the opportunity to focus on work as their leading motivation for coming into the office. The commentary argues office setups are often \"simply not competitive with what's available to employees at home,\" that hot-desking creates unwanted proximity to unfamiliar deskmates, and that employees value predictability and consistency in their workspace. Named Korn Ferry contributors are Mark Royal, Ph.D. (Senior Client Partner), Maria Amato (Senior Client Partner), and Tamara Rodman (Senior Client Partner, Culture, Change & Communications)."
  },
  {
    "source_id": "SRC-003",
    "title": "2024 Americas Office Occupier Sentiment Survey",
    "authors_or_organization": "CBRE Research",
    "publication_date": "2024-08-13",
    "journal_or_venue": "CBRE (global commercial real estate services firm)",
    "doi": null,
    "url": "https://www.cbre.com/insights/reports/2024-americas-office-occupier-sentiment-survey",
    "source_type": "INDUSTRY_SURVEY_REPORT",
    "access_status": "FULL_TEXT_ACCESSIBLE",
    "retrieval_method": "DIRECT_FETCH_KNOWN_URL_NOT_SEARCH",
    "fetched_extraction": "CBRE's 2024 Americas Office Occupier Sentiment Survey, based on responses from 225 corporate real estate executives across the U.S., Canada, and Latin America (survey conducted May 2024, report published 2024-08-13), reports that only 40% of surveyed companies had an employee-to-desk ratio of 1.0:1 or less in 2024, down from 56% the year before (2023); the survey's respondents expect that share to fall further, to roughly one-third of companies, within the following two years (by 2026). Sector-level average desk ratios were 1.6:1 for financial services in 2024 (projected 1.8:1 by 2026) and 1.7:1 for technology in 2024 (projected 2.1:1 by 2026) -- i.e., desk sharing is expected to intensify overall even as some individual employers reverse course toward assigned seating. The same survey found approximately 80% of organizations have a return-to-office policy (up slightly from 78% in 2023), but only 17% actively enforce it; 51% of employers formally mandate a minimum number of in-office days while only 45% measure actual attendance. 60% of employers want employees in the office 3 or more days per week, but only 51% of employees actually attend that often (average employer expectation 3.1 days/week overall vs. average employee attendance 2.8 days/week). 42% of respondents said flexible office space already exceeds 10% of their portfolio (up from 36% in 2023), and 58% expect it to exceed 10% within two years."
  }
]
